stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: For decades, a rail line through the center of Tallmere carried freight past warehouses that had long since closed. In 2019, the city converted the abandoned corridor into a four-mile greenway, ______ residents with a car-free route linking three neighborhoods that had previously been divided by the tracks. Within two years, counts showed that more than 3,000 people used the path on an average weekday.
explanation: The sentence already has a subject and main verb: "the city converted." What follows the comma is a descriptive add-on telling what the conversion did, so it needs a participle, not another tensed verb. "Providing" is the "-ing" form because the conversion causes the result, and it attaches cleanly to the clause before it.

B.why: You added a second tensed verb, "provides," after "converted" with no conjunction joining them. Without "and," two main verbs can't sit side by side, and the present tense also clashes with the past-tense "converted."

C.why: "It provides" is a complete independent clause. Putting it after a comma with no conjunction creates a comma splice. You needed a modifier here, not a new sentence.

D.why: "Has provided" is a finite verb competing with "converted" for the same subject, and nothing like "and" connects them. The main clause was already complete, so the blank needed a participle.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Lake-effect snow develops when frigid air moves across a large body of water that has not yet frozen. As it travels, the air absorbs heat and moisture from the lake's surface, ______ towering bands of cloud that can bury downwind towns under more than a foot of snow in a single afternoon. Forecasters track wind direction closely, since a small shift can move the heaviest snowfall many miles.
explanation: The main clause is already complete: "the air absorbs heat and moisture." The blank begins a phrase describing the result of that absorption, so it calls for a participle. "Building" is the "-ing" form because the clause before it causes the cloud bands to form.

B.why: "Builds" gives "air" a second main verb with no "and" to connect it to "absorbs." The clause already had its verb, so the blank couldn't hold another tensed one.

C.why: "It builds" starts a new independent clause, and joining two independent clauses with only a comma is a comma splice.

D.why: "Were building" is a finite verb whose plural form doesn't match the singular "air." Even if it agreed, it would still be an unconnected second main verb. The sentence needed a bare participle.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Printmaker Ingrid Valtersen often limited herself to a handful of inks. Her woodblock print The Salt Marsh, ______ from three blocks of cherry wood in 1931, uses only gray, ochre, and a pale green, yet it conveys the shifting light of an entire coastal morning. Collectors have long admired how much the image achieves with so little color.
explanation: The subject is "Her woodblock print The Salt Marsh," and its main verb, "uses," comes after the second comma. The phrase between the commas just describes the print, so it needs a participle. The print received the carving, so you need the "-ed" form: "carved."

B.why: "Was carved" makes the interrupting phrase into a second main verb for the print. The sentence's real verb, "uses," comes later, so a tensed verb in the blank leaves two main verbs with nothing linking them.

C.why: "It was carved" drops a complete clause into the middle of the sentence and cuts the subject off from its verb, "uses." The result is an ungrammatical fused sentence.

D.why: "Has been carved" is a finite verb, so it competes with "uses" for the same subject. The time marker "in 1931" also rules out the present perfect. A bare participle is all the phrase needs.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Corn draws heavily on soil nitrogen, so most growers apply synthetic fertilizer every season. At an experimental farm in eastern Nebraska, researchers instead planted strips of crimson clover between the corn rows, ______ the amount of fertilizer the crop needed by nearly a third. The clover's roots host bacteria that convert nitrogen from the air into a form plants can absorb.
explanation: "Researchers ... planted" is already a complete main clause. The words after the comma describe the effect of the planting, so the blank needs a participle. "Reducing" is the "-ing" form because the planting caused the drop in fertilizer.

B.why: "Reduces" is a singular present-tense verb that doesn't match the plural "researchers" or the past tense of "planted." It also adds a second main verb with no conjunction.

C.why: "They reduced" is an independent clause, and attaching it with only a comma creates a comma splice. The blank needed a modifier, not a new clause.

D.why: "Were reducing" is a finite verb placed next to "planted" without "and" to join them. The clause already had its verb, so the blank should be a bare participle.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Bar-tailed godwits are known for crossing the Pacific Ocean in a single flight. One young bird, ______ with a lightweight satellite transmitter on an Alaskan mudflat, traveled roughly 12,800 kilometers to New Zealand over eleven days without once stopping to feed or rest. Ornithologists believe the birds rely on fat reserves that can make up more than half of their body weight at departure.
explanation: The subject is "One young bird," and its main verb, "traveled," comes after the second comma. The phrase in between only describes the bird, so it takes a participle. The bird received the transmitter, so the "-ed" form "fitted" is correct.

B.why: "Was fitted" gives "bird" one tensed verb and "traveled" gives it another, with no conjunction joining them. The real main verb was still coming, so the blank didn't need one.

C.why: "It was fitted" puts a whole independent clause between the subject and "traveled," which breaks the sentence. A descriptive phrase can't contain its own subject and verb like this.

D.why: "Fits" is a finite present-tense verb, so it clashes with the past-tense account and adds an unconnected second main verb. The bird is also the one receiving the action here, so the form must be the participle "fitted."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Archaeologist Rosa Quispe and her team spent three seasons excavating a hillside settlement in southern Peru. In their final season, they uncovered a sealed storage room holding forty clay jars ______ with dried maize, beans, and squash seeds. The find suggests that the settlement's residents stored food carefully against years of poor harvest.
explanation: The sentence already has its subject and main verb: 'they uncovered.' The blank starts a description of the jars. The jars received the packing, so you need the bare past participle 'packed.' 'Jars packed with dried maize' works as a modifier and adds no second verb.

A.why: 'Were packed' is a tensed verb. It would give the jars their own main verb with no conjunction or 'that' to join it to 'they uncovered,' so the sentence becomes a run-on. You probably read 'jars were packed' as a full clause without checking that the sentence already had a main verb.

C.why: 'Are packed' is a second tensed verb with nothing to join it to the main clause, and its present tense also clashes with the past-tense passage. You may have checked only that 'jars are' agrees and forgot to count the verbs.

D.why: 'Have been packed' is still a tensed verb phrase. It gives the jars a main verb of their own and fuses two clauses with no connecting word. It sounds formal, but the sentence already had 'uncovered' as its main verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Along the coast of southeastern Alaska, sea otters eat enormous numbers of sea urchins, ______ the urchin population small enough for kelp forests to regrow. Where otters were hunted out in the nineteenth century, urchins multiplied and grazed the kelp down to bare rock, leaving fish and seabirds with far less shelter.
explanation: 'Sea otters eat' is already a complete main clause. The blank begins an add-on that describes what the eating does. Because the action in the first clause causes the result, you need the '-ing' participle: 'keeping the urchin population small.'

A.why: 'This keeps' brings in a new subject and verb, which makes a second independent clause joined to the first with only a comma. That is a comma splice. You may have chosen it because 'this' seemed to name the effect clearly.

B.why: 'They keep' is a full new clause attached with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. You probably liked having a clear subject and missed that the sentence already had one with its own verb.

C.why: 'Keeps' is a tensed verb with no subject of its own. It can't attach to 'otters,' which is plural and already has the verb 'eat.' You may have heard 'urchins, keeps' as a continuation without checking what the verb belongs to.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Before 1880, most charts of the Orinoco delta showed only a handful of navigable channels. Mapmaker Inés Alvarado's survey of the region, ______ on foot and by canoe over two wet seasons, recorded more than three hundred channels that earlier charts had missed entirely.
explanation: The subject is 'survey' and its main verb is 'recorded,' which comes after the second comma. The part between the commas only describes the survey, and the survey received the action, so the bare participle 'conducted' fits. It is set off by commas at both ends.

B.why: 'Was conducted' would make 'survey... was conducted' a full clause, and then 'recorded' would be a second main verb with no conjunction. You may have thought the subject still needed its verb because you didn't read on to 'recorded.'

C.why: 'It was conducted' drops a complete clause into the middle of the sentence with only commas around it. That splits the subject 'survey' from its verb 'recorded' and fuses two clauses. You probably wanted a clear subject for the description.

D.why: 'Had been conducted' is a tensed verb. It competes with 'recorded' for the role of main verb, and nothing joins the two. The past perfect sounded right next to 'before 1880,' but the slot needs a modifier, not a verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The seismometers at a monitoring station outside Wellington, New Zealand, measure ground motion one hundred times per second, ______ records detailed enough to tell a distant earthquake apart from the rumble of passing trucks. Researchers use these records to refine estimates of where future quakes are most likely to start.
explanation: 'The seismometers... measure' is the complete main clause. The blank begins a description of what that measuring yields. The seismometers are doing the producing, so the '-ing' participle 'producing' is the one that adds information without creating a second main verb.

A.why: 'They produce' starts a second independent clause joined only by a comma, which makes a comma splice. You may have wanted to restate the subject so the action was clear.

B.why: 'Produces' is a singular tensed verb with no subject that matches it. The plural 'seismometers' already has its verb, 'measure.' You may have matched it to the nearby singular noun 'second.'

D.why: Followed by the object 'records,' 'produced' acts as a past-tense main verb, not a modifier. That gives the sentence a second verb with no conjunction, and it also clashes with the present tense. You probably read 'produced records' as a natural phrase without counting verbs.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Economist Tomás Reyes wanted to know why turnover in warehouse jobs runs so high. In a 2023 study, he tracked 1,200 workers ______ by a regional shipping firm. He found that workers given a predictable weekly schedule were about half as likely to quit within a year as those whose hours changed with little notice.
explanation: 'He tracked 1,200 workers' already has its subject and main verb. The blank starts a description of the workers. They were hired by the firm, so they received the action, and you need the bare past participle 'employed.'

A.why: 'Were employed' gives 'workers' a tensed verb of its own with no 'who' or conjunction to link it. That puts two clauses into one sentence with no connector. You may have read 'workers were employed' as a complete thought.

B.why: 'Are employed' adds a second tensed verb with no linking word, and its present tense also clashes with the past-tense study. You likely checked agreement with 'workers' but didn't count the verbs already in the sentence.

C.why: 'They were employed' is a full independent clause run straight into the first one with no punctuation or conjunction, which makes a fused sentence. You may have added 'they' to make the description sound complete.
